items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.summary: Maximum inner product search (MIPS) sits at the core of recommendation systems, search, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Given a query vector, MIPS systems search within a database of millions of candidate key vectors for the one that best matches the query. The original data point associated with that best-matching key is then used to handle the query: in RAG, the document that is best suited to answer the question is typically prefixed to the query. [...] — a signal that generic, query-agnostic methods leave untapped. Crafting methods that work best for a likely source of inputs — rather than aiming for good performance on all possible inputs — is a central tenet of modern machine learning that helps redirect compute resources more efficiently. items.title: Escaping the Cloud with Edge RAG – Communications of the ACM
items.summary:
In a traditional cloud-based RAG setup, a software architect relies on heavy, deep-learning transformer models (like BERT) to generate text embeddings, which are then stored in a massive, centralized vector database. If you attempt to replicate this naive architecture on a smartphone—trying to load a 3GB embedding model simultaneously alongside a 3GB language model—the application will instantly crash. By mastering local RAG and the MLX framework on the mobile edge, we can finally resolve the privacy-utility paradox—delivering uncompromising, intelligent financial advisory with absolute data sovereignty.
